solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Bad appetite sharing large helping on plate

indicators.note: on says the helping is placed after what comes before it
sharing says the two words overlap on one common letter, so that letter appears once

parts.note: ill means bad, as in ill effects
lust is a strong appetite or craving
L is the standard abbreviation for large, as on clothing labels
a ration is a portion or helping of food

explanation.surface: A greedy diner with a poor appetite, or a big appetite, piling food onto a plate.
explanation.walkthrough: ILL and LUST overlap on their shared L to give ILLUST; 'sharing' signals the overlap. 'Plate' is a full-page picture in a book.
explanation.definitionFit: A plate is a printed picture in a book, usually on glossy paper, so it is a kind of picture.

clue.text: Due to get Marks and Spencer briefs …

parts.note: to be in for something is to be due to get it, as in 'in for a shock'
M&S is the everyday abbreviation for the British department store Marks and Spencer

explanation.surface: Someone is about to buy some underpants from Marks and Spencer, continuing into the next clue.
explanation.walkthrough: Marks and Spencer is a British high-street store famous for its underwear. 'Briefs' looks like underpants but is the verb.
explanation.definitionFit: To brief someone is to give them instructions or information, which is to tell them the facts.

clue.text: … underwear's new range, top to bottom

definitions.note: the 's stands for is, linking the definition to the wordplay

indicators.note: in a down entry the top letter is taken from the start and put at the foot of the word

parts.note: a line is a range of products, as in a clothing line

explanation.surface: Continuing the shopping trip: the store's new underwear range, from top to bottom.
explanation.walkthrough: N plus LINE gives NLINE; 'top to bottom' moves the N to the end.
explanation.definitionFit: Linen is an old general term for underclothes and other garments once made of flax cloth.

clue.text: Start to sell show for the audience?

definitions.text: Start to sell show for the audience?

indicators.note: the start of a word is its first letter, so only the opening letter of sell is used
an audience hears rather than reads, so the letters are taken by their sound

parts.note: to indicate is to show or point out; said aloud, the word is heard with the same sounds as the spelling with a Y

explanation.surface: A producer begins to market a television show to the viewing public.
explanation.walkthrough: S plus INDICATE sounds like the answer. The whole clue also describes the action: selling a programme to many broadcasters.
explanation.definitionFit: To syndicate a show is to sell it to many broadcasters or papers at once so it reaches a wide audience.

clue.text: Gunners one down, as you'd recognise, and bust

parts.note: the Royal Artillery, the British army's gunners, are the RA
I is the Roman numeral for one
D for down is a crossword convention, as solvers will recognise

explanation.surface: Gunners lose a man and crash out, as you'd recognise from the scoreline.
explanation.walkthrough: 'As you'd recognise' nods to D for down being a crossword convention rather than a common abbreviation. Gunners is also the nickname of Arsenal football club.
explanation.definitionFit: A bust is slang for a police swoop on premises, the same as a police raid.

clue.text: What makes seasoned sailor? Previously being in Navy

parts.note: tar is an old word for a sailor

indicators.note: being in says the word for previously sits inside the letters for the navy

parts.note: RN is the Royal Navy
ago means previously, in the past

explanation.surface: A riddle about what turns a sailor into an old hand, answered by earlier service in the navy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Seasoned sailor' reads as an old salt, but 'seasoned' belongs to the definition: the herb seasons food.
explanation.definitionFit: This aniseed-flavoured herb is used to season food, so it is something that makes dishes seasoned.

clue.text: Slaughter and cut everyone's entrails

parts.note: to off someone is slang for to kill or slaughter them

indicators.note: cut says the word loses its last letter

parts.note: all means everyone; the 's is a link

explanation.surface: A butcher kills and dresses an animal, removing its innards.
explanation.walkthrough: ALL cut short gives AL.
explanation.definitionFit: Offal is the edible innards of a slaughtered animal, so it covers the entrails.

clue.text: Irritating when catching supporter in view, oddly

indicators.note: catching says the word for when holds the supporter inside it

parts.note: as can mean when, as in 'as I left'
a bra is a supporting undergarment

indicators.note: oddly picks the first, third and fifth letters of in view

explanation.surface: Someone finds it irritating when a support garment is visible.
explanation.walkthrough: AS holds BRA to give ABRAS; the odd letters of 'in view' give IVE.
explanation.definitionFit: An abrasive manner is harsh and grating, which is irritating to others.

clue.text: As blackbird is cooked and pie finally eaten

indicators.note: eaten says that letter is swallowed inside the word for cooked

parts.note: baked means cooked in an oven

indicators.note: finally takes the closing letter of pie

explanation.surface: The nursery rhyme's four and twenty blackbirds, baked in a pie and finally eaten.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface recalls 'Sing a Song of Sixpence', where blackbirds are baked in a pie.
explanation.definitionFit: A blackbird has a bill, so it is a bird with a beak, describing how it is formed.

clue.text: One enthusiastic about business centre?

indicators.note: about says the enthusiast wraps around those middle letters

parts.note: a fancier is an enthusiast, as in pigeon fancier

indicators.note: centre picks the middle two letters of business

explanation.surface: A riddle: who is keen on the City, the centre of business?
explanation.walkthrough: FANCIER goes about IN, the centre of 'business'. The whole clue also defines a money man keen on business.
explanation.definitionFit: A person who deals in large-scale money matters is devoted to commerce, keen on business and found in its centres.

clue.text: Sort of a bleeding heart story

indicators.note: heart says the letters come from inside the run of words, not from their ends

explanation.surface: A sentimental, bleeding-heart kind of tale.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sort of' reads as a qualifier for the story, but those words are part of the letters searched.
explanation.definitionFit: A fable is a short moral tale, often with animals, so it is a kind of tale.

clue.text: French director on the subject of film style

parts.note: re means concerning or on the subject of
noir is the dark, shadowy style of crime film

explanation.surface: A note about a French film-maker's view of a certain cinematic style.
explanation.definitionFit: Jean Renoir was a celebrated French film-maker, son of the painter Pierre-Auguste.

clue.text: Rough break ends keeping perfect standard

indicators.note: keeping says the end letters hold the other pieces between them
ends takes the first and last letters of break

parts.note: all can mean perfect or complete, as in 'all correct'
par is a standard or norm

explanation.surface: A rough patch: a break that ends up keeping a perfect standard.
explanation.walkthrough: B and K hold ALL and PAR. The definition is an American usage, as in a ballpark figure.
explanation.definitionFit: A ballpark estimate is an approximate one, so it means approximate in that adjectival use.

clue.text: Covert organisation in virtually traded group

indicators.note: this word is a container marker: it says one piece is placed inside the other, and the clue words of the pieces show which way round
virtually means almost, so the word loses its last letter

parts.note: sold means traded
the CIA is the US intelligence agency

explanation.surface: A secret organisation that has infiltrated a group of traders.
explanation.walkthrough: SOL (traded almost) holds CIA.
explanation.definitionFit: A social is an informal party or gathering of club members, a group meeting together.

clue.text: State of US flag, flapping

parts.note: a regiment's flag is its colours, here in the US spelling to suit the state
flapping is a state of fuss or agitation, which is ado

explanation.surface: The condition of the American flag, fluttering in the wind.
explanation.walkthrough: 'State of US flag' reads as one phrase about the flag; the definition stops at 'US'. 'In a flap' means flustered.
explanation.definitionFit: This mountainous western state is one of the fifty that make up the United States.

clue.text: Softened, and second, faded around mid-life

parts.note: mo is a short moment, a second

indicators.note: around says the word for faded wraps those middle letters

parts.note: died can mean faded away, as a sound dies

indicators.note: mid says only the middle two letters of the word life are used

explanation.surface: Someone mellowed, and quickly faded, around middle age.
explanation.definitionFit: Modified means altered, often toned down, so a view that is tempered or moderated.

clue.text: Dessert in pieces in cool sauce

indicators.note: the second in says that combination goes inside the word for cool

parts.note: ice is a cooling thing; ice and cool both mean chill

indicators.note: in says the dessert goes inside the pieces

parts.note: men are pieces in chess or draughts
pud is short for pudding, a dessert

explanation.surface: A pudding, broken into pieces, swimming in cold sauce.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sauce' looks like the topping for the dessert, but it is the definition in its sense of cheek.
explanation.definitionFit: Sauce is informal for cheek or insolence, the same as impertinent boldness.

clue.text: Following turn to toilet, endlessly avoid paper

parts.note: F is the abbreviation for following, as in page references

indicators.note: turn says the toilet word is read backwards

parts.note: loo is a British word for toilet

indicators.note: endlessly says both outer letters are removed

parts.note: to escape something is to avoid it

explanation.surface: After a visit to the toilet, someone avoids the paper; a toilet-humour scene.
explanation.walkthrough: F, OOL (LOO turned) and SCAP (ESCAPE without its ends). 'Paper' looks like toilet paper but means a size of writing paper.
explanation.definitionFit: Foolscap is a traditional large size of writing or printing sheet, named after an old watermark.

clue.text: Congregation's beliefs overturned creating fuss

parts.note: a fold is a church congregation, a flock; the 's is a link

indicators.note: overturned says the word is read backwards

parts.note: lore is a body of traditional beliefs

explanation.surface: A church's doctrines are overthrown, causing a commotion.
explanation.definitionFit: Folderol means needless fuss or nonsense, frivolous commotion over nothing.

clue.text: Beds town losing head in football season openers

indicators.note: in says the shortened town sits between those two opening letters
openers takes the first letter of each of football and season
losing head says the town drops its first letter

parts.note: Luton is a town in Bedfordshire with a football club

explanation.surface: A Bedfordshire town relegated at the start of the football season.
explanation.walkthrough: UTON goes between F and S. Beds is short for Bedfordshire, Luton's county, a fitting misdirection.
explanation.definitionFit: Futons are Japanese-style mattresses used on the floor or on a frame, so they are things to sleep on.

clue.text: Most fit turning in pursuit set pace

indicators.note: turning says the hidden letters are read backwards
the clue word that says the letters sit inside the next words

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: The fittest cyclist, turning in a pursuit race, sets the pace.
explanation.walkthrough: 'In' marks the letters as hidden in 'pursuit set pace'; 'turning' reads them backwards.
explanation.definitionFit: Apt means suitable or fitting, so the superlative is the most suitable.

clue.text: Adornments of dancers, less attractive flipping

indicators.note: flipping says the hidden letters are read backwards
the clue word that says the letters sit inside the next words

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: Ornaments on dancers who are less attractive, whirling about.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Of' marks the letters as hidden in 'dancers, less attractive'; 'flipping' reads them backwards.
explanation.definitionFit: Tassels are hanging tufts of threads used as decoration on clothing and furnishings.

clue.text: Suppress article about resistance facing extreme Left

indicators.note: about says the article goes around the other pieces

parts.note: the is the definite article
R is the symbol for electrical resistance
OTT, over the top, means extreme

explanation.surface: A newspaper suppresses an article about resistance from the far Left.
explanation.walkthrough: THE goes about R, OTT and L. 'Article' suggests a press piece but means the word 'the'.
explanation.definitionFit: To throttle is to strangle or choke, and figuratively to stifle or quash something.

clue.text: Half-loathe Conservatives' wing protecting 'one of them'

indicators.note: protecting says the other letters surround the numeral
half here takes the back three letters of the six-letter word loathe

parts.note: the Conservatives are the party of the right wing, R
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: A half-hearted dislike of the Tory right protecting someone seen as one of their own.
explanation.definitionFit: This possessive word means belonging to those people, the same as 'of them'.

clue.text: Police back breaking heartless establishment's laws

indicators.note: breaking says the police letters split the outer letters
heartless removes the inside letters of the word, leaving its first and last plus the S

parts.note: the word establishment with its 's

indicators.note: back says the letters are read in reverse

parts.note: CID is the Criminal Investigation Department of the British police

explanation.surface: Police raid a heartless institution for breaking its rules.
explanation.walkthrough: CID turned is DIC; 'establishment' heartless gives ET, and the 's adds S, so DIC breaks E and TS.
explanation.definitionFit: Edicts are official decrees issued by an authority, so they are rules or laws.

clue.text: Song of praise by Church member elevated belief

indicators.note: elevated says the letters go upwards, read backwards in a down entry

parts.note: an ode is a lyric poem of praise
RC is a Roman Catholic, a member of that church

explanation.surface: A hymn from a churchgoer raises up their faith.
explanation.definitionFit: A credo is a statement of faith, from the Latin for 'I believe'.

clue.text: Boarding house possibly takes in

definitions.meaning: lodgings, such as a rented room in a boarding house
understands or grasps, as in the slang 'I dig it'

explanation.surface: A boarding house might take in lodgers.
explanation.definitionFit: Digs is British slang for lodgings, and to dig something is slang for to understand it.

clue.text: Bump and grind, initially naked?

indicators.note: and joins the letter to the word, placing it inside the word for naked

parts.note: nude means naked

indicators.note: initially takes the first letter of grind

explanation.surface: A striptease: bump and grind, with the dancer ending up naked.
explanation.walkthrough: G goes inside NUDE. 'Bump and grind' is a burlesque dance phrase.
explanation.definitionFit: A nudge is a light push or prod with the elbow, a small knock or bump.

clue.text: Regulars, right before time, almost preferred returning outside

indicators.note: outside says the reversed letters wrap around the other pieces
returning says those letters are read backwards
almost says the word loses its final letter

parts.note: elect means chosen or preferred, as in the bride-elect

indicators.note: before says the right comes ahead of the time

parts.note: a lien is a legal right to hold property until a debt is paid

explanation.surface: Regular customers, the right ones, arrive early and the favoured come back.
explanation.walkthrough: ELEC turned gives CELE, which goes outside LIEN and T.
explanation.definitionFit: A clientele is the body of customers who regularly use a shop or service.

clue.text: Incredible writer nearly consuming last of madeleine, notice

indicators.note: consuming says the writer's letters swallow the other pieces
nearly says the name loses its final letter

parts.note: Marcel Proust, the French novelist

indicators.note: last of takes the final letter of madeleine

parts.note: a poster is a notice put up in public

explanation.surface: Proust eating his famous madeleine cake, which set off his memories in his novel.
explanation.walkthrough: PROUS holds E and POSTER. Proust's madeleine dipped in tea is the novel's famous memory trigger.
explanation.definitionFit: Preposterous means absurd or outrageous, beyond belief, so it means unbelievable.
